title: Paul VI (1963–1978)
hookLine: the pope who boarded planes to Jerusalem, India and New York, and told the United Nations no more war

lines: A MAN IN WHITE IN NEW YORK.
cards: A thin man in white walks to a podium in New York. Before him sit the representatives of the world's nations, in the hall of the United Nations General Assembly. He is the bishop of Rome, a long way from Rome.
He came by plane. He has no army and no vote in this hall, and he tells them he has nothing to ask for himself. Then, speaking in French, he says the words this day is built on.
No more war. War never again. His name was Giovanni Battista Montini.
As pope he was called Paul the Sixth.

teach.h: THE POPE WHO FINISHED THE COUNCIL.
teach.b: Paul the Sixth came right after Good Pope John, and he's easy to overlook. First, the finisher.
John called the council; Paul was elected between its sessions, with much of its work still ahead, and he brought it to its close and began putting it into practice.
The Mass in local languages from yesterday came in under him. Second, the traveler.

teach.h: THE TRAVELER: JERUSALEM, INDIA, NEW YORK.
teach.b: He took the name of Paul, the apostle who crossed the sea again and again, and he got on airplanes: to Jerusalem, where he embraced the Orthodox patriarch Athenagoras, to India, to New York. Third, the speech.

teach.h: AT THE UN: NO MORE WAR.
teach.b: At the United Nations he called himself an expert in humanity, a man with long experience of human beings, and he begged the nations: no more war, war never again.
If they wanted to be brothers, he told them, let the weapons fall from their hands.

Catholics hear in this Isaiah's old promise, in the Douay-Rheims: "nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they be exercised any more to war." Fourth, the cost. His years weren't calm.
Some of his teaching, especially his letter on marriage and birth control, was hard for some Catholics to accept, and it's still argued over.

teach.h: NATION SHALL NOT LIFT UP SWORD AGAINST NATION.
teach.b: The Church has since named him a saint. What stays is a man without an army, standing in a hall of flags, asking the nations to put the weapons down.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Paul VI, and the Holy See keeps a permanent observer at the United Nations, where later popes have also addressed the General Assembly.

games.q: you're Paul VI, invited to speak to the nations of the world. you have one speech. what is at its heart?
o: a plea: no more war, war never again.
a list of the nations to blame.
games.why: he asked for nothing for himself and begged the nations: no more war, war never again.

practice: Picture that hall, a country's name on each card, and then the people behind the cards: diplomats who haven't slept, translators in their booths, peacekeepers far from home, staff who feed refugees.
Pick one of them and stay with that person a while. If you pray, pray for them, perhaps with Isaiah's line about swords; if not, wish them steady hands.
